articles.title: Beta SDKs for the 2026-07-28 MCP Spec Release Candidate Are Here
articles.summary: Beta SDKs for Python, TypeScript, Go, and C# are available for the 2026-07-28 MCP spec release candidate. This allows developers to test and migrate their servers before the spec goes final on July 28.

articles.title: Space Recognition with LiDAR and Edge Impulse
articles.summary: Train models on real-time LiDAR data to recognize rooms and spaces using Edge Impulse. This enables robots to navigate without cameras, GPS, or maps.

articles.title: Computer-Use and TOCTOU: What You Click Is Not What You Get!
articles.summary: A researcher reproduced a vulnerability in ChatGPT Operator by exploiting a race condition, allowing them to manipulate the model's output. This matters because it highlights the potential for attacks on AI systems through subtle manipulation of user input.

articles.title: Edge Aware Real-Time Security (EARS)
articles.summary: Edge Impulse's EARS tool activates recording on security cameras and analyzes contents locally for potential threats. This matters as it enables real-time security monitoring and response on edge devices.

articles.title: Your Smartphone is a Portable Multimodal DAQ for Edge AI
articles.summary: Android Data Collector turns a smartphone into a portable multimodal data acquisition platform, capable of collecting data from various sources. This enables developers to collect and analyze data from multiple sources, facilitating the development of edge AI applications.

articles.title: Enterprise-Managed Authorization: Zero-touch OAuth for MCP
articles.summary: The Enterprise-Managed Authorization extension to MCP is now stable, allowing organizations to centrally provision MCP server access through their identity provider.

articles.title: Exploring Physical AI: On-Device Vision for ROS-Based Embodied Robots
articles.summary: A humanoid robot uses Edge Impulse and ROS 2 for on-device ball tracking and autonomous movement. This matters because it demonstrates the potential for real-time AI on edge devices in robotics applications.

articles.title: How to Build Cost-Effective Edge AI for Quality & Failure Detection
articles.summary: Edge Impulse and a $100 Rubik Pi 3 enable real-time visual anomaly detection for manufacturers of any size.

articles.title: Helping Patients Communicate Through On-Device Gesture Recognition
articles.summary: A wearable device uses TinyML to recognize hand gestures, enabling patients to communicate quickly and privately. This technology matters because it provides a new way for patients to interact with their environment without relying on verbal communication.

articles.title: The 2026-07-28 MCP Specification Release Candidate
articles.summary: The MCP specification release candidate includes a stateless protocol core, Extensions framework, Tasks, MCP Apps, and authorization hardening, with a formal deprecation policy. This matters because it outlines the next version of the MCP protocol, which enables standardized communication between AI models and their contexts.

articles.title: Memory Is a Feature. It Is Also an Attack Surface
articles.summary: OWASP highlights the risk of memory and context poisoning in AI agents, which can carry untrusted input forward, making it a new attack surface.

articles.title: Copirate 365 at DEF CON: Plundering in the Depths of Microsoft Copilot (CVE-2026-24299)
articles.summary: A researcher disclosed vulnerabilities in Microsoft Copilot, including CVE-2026-24299, which have been patched by Microsoft. This matters because it highlights the potential security risks of AI-powered tools and the importance of responsible disclosure.

articles.title: Sequoia Ascent 2026 summary
articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy discusses the shift in AI agents, calling it an 'agentic inflection point', where LLMs are becoming a new programmable layer for digital work, and the programmer's role is evolving to an orchestrator of agents.

articles.title: Project Deal: our Claude-run marketplace experiment
articles.summary: Anthropic ran a week-long experiment, Project Deal, where AI agents (Claude) negotiated transactions between employees, resulting in 186 deals worth over $4,000. This pilot experiment suggests AI agents could soon play a significant role in commercial exchange.

articles.title: Breaking Opus 4.7 with ChatGPT (Hacking Claude's Memory)
articles.summary: ChatGPT generated an adversarial image that tricked Claude Opus 4.7 into invoking a memory tool and persisting false memories. This matters because even a more resilient model like Opus 4.7 can still be vulnerable to such attacks.

articles.title: FinBot CTF Is Live: A Hands-On Companion to the OWASP GenAI Security Project
articles.summary: OWASP GenAI Security Project launched FinBot, a hands-on CTF environment for exploring agentic AI risks in a simulated financial services application. This interactive platform allows builders and defenders to test their skills in a live, multi-agent system.

articles.title: OWASP GenAI Exploit Round-up Report Q1 2026
articles.summary: OWASP GenAI Security Project published a report on major AI-related security incidents from Q1 2026, including incidents not intended to be exhaustive. This report highlights the ongoing threat landscape for AI security.

articles.title: Given Enough Agents, All Bugs Become Shallow
articles.summary: Agents are becoming highly effective at finding security vulnerabilities in code, allowing for rapid analysis and potentially uncovering all bugs with sufficient resources.

articles.title: Expanding the MCP Maintainer Team
articles.summary: The MCP governance team has expanded with a new Lead Maintainer and an additional Core Maintainer as the project continues to grow.

articles.title: The making of Claude Code
articles.summary: Anthropic's blog post details the development of Claude Code, a large language model framework. This matters because it provides insight into the design and architecture of a leading AI model framework.

articles.title: OWASP GenAI Security Project Expands AI Security Frameworks Ahead of RSA 2026, Celebrates Continued Sponsor Support
articles.summary: The OWASP GenAI Security Project has expanded its AI security frameworks and will participate in a week of RSA programming, highlighting growing industry adoption and support.

articles.title: Agent Commander: Promptware-Powered Command and Control
articles.summary: Researchers have developed promptware-powered command and control (C2) tools, which use complex prompt-injection payloads to abuse AI models for malicious purposes. This development highlights the growing threat of AI-powered attacks.

articles.title: Tool Annotations as Risk Vocabulary: What Hints Can and Can't Do
articles.summary: The MCP community has proposed five new tool annotations to describe tool behavior, driven by a better understanding of risk in agentic workflows. This matters because it could improve the safety and reliability of AI systems by providing clearer information about tool behavior.

articles.title: Understanding MCP Extensions
articles.summary: The MCP Blog provides a guide to MCP extensions, explaining how they build on the core protocol and highlighting community patterns.

articles.title: The 2026 MCP Roadmap
articles.summary: The 2026 MCP Roadmap outlines key areas of focus, including transport scalability, agent communication, governance maturation, and enterprise readiness.

articles.title: Scary Agent Skills: Hidden Unicode Instructions in Skills ...And How To Catch Them
articles.summary: A hidden prompt injection vulnerability in Skills allows backdooring with invisible Unicode characters, which can be interpreted by models like Gemini and Claude. This matters because it introduces a new attack surface for Skills, potentially allowing malicious updates to be injected undetected.

articles.title: OpenAI Explains URL-Based Data Exfiltration Mitigations in New Paper
articles.summary: OpenAI published a paper on mitigating URL-based data exfiltration in language-model agents, detailing new security measures. This matters because it shows OpenAI's increased transparency and effort to address security vulnerabilities in their models.

articles.title: The first AI-planned drive on Mars
articles.summary: Anthropic's Claude AI model helped plan the first AI-planned drive on Mars, navigating a 400-meter path through rocks on the Martian surface. This marks a significant step in using AI for space exploration, where human operators can't micromanage due to signal delays.

articles.title: MCP Apps - Bringing UI Capabilities To MCP Clients
articles.summary: MCP Apps is now live, allowing tools to return interactive UI components that render directly in conversations. This enables more interactive and user-friendly experiences for MCP clients.

articles.title: January MCP Core Maintainer Update
articles.summary: The MCP Core Maintainer team has undergone changes for 2026, with departing members and new additions, and a focus on MCP governance.

articles.title: Minting Next.js Authentication Cookies
articles.summary: An adversary can mint authentication cookies for Next.js applications, allowing persistent access as any user, due to a deserialization vulnerability.

articles.title: 2025 LLM Year in Review
articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy reviews the 2025 LLM landscape, highlighting two paradigm changes: Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) and the shift from thinking of LLMs as 'evolving animals' to 'summoning ghosts'.

articles.title: Exploring the Future of MCP Transports
articles.summary: The Transport Working Group is planning to evolve MCP beyond Streamable HTTP for enterprise-scale remote deployments.

articles.title: Evolving AI Transparency: The Journey of the AIBOM Generator and Its New Home at OWASP
articles.summary: OWASP introduced an open-source tool to generate AI Software Bills of Materials (AIBOM) for Hugging Face models, sparking interest in AI transparency and software supply chain security.

articles.title: Chemical hygiene
articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy shares his guide to chemical hygiene, focusing on water and air purification, and recommends specific products and methods for improvement.

articles.title: Auto-grading decade-old Hacker News discussions with hindsight
articles.summary: Karpathy explores the idea of using LLMs to auto-grade decade-old Hacker News discussions with hindsight, as a thought exercise on scaling and retrospectively analyzing human historical data.

articles.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications – The Benchmark for Agentic Security in the Age of Autonomous AI
articles.summary: OWASP released the Top 10 for Agentic AI Applications, a framework for securing autonomous AI systems, based on real incidents and industry adoption. This benchmark aims to advance the security of Agentic Applications at the pace of innovation.

articles.title: OWASP GenAI Security Project Releases Top 10 Risks and Mitigations for Agentic AI Security
articles.summary: OWASP GenAI Security Project released a list of top 10 risks and mitigations for agentic AI security, compiled from over 100 industry leaders' input and published resources. This guidance aims to help address critical security risks in generative and agentic AI.

articles.title: MCP joins the Agentic AI Foundation
articles.summary: MCP is being donated to the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation for vendor-neutral governance.

articles.title: The Normalization of Deviance in AI
articles.summary: The AI industry may be normalizing the over-reliance on LLM outputs, a cultural failure that can lead to catastrophic consequences. This matters because it could lead to a repeat of past disasters, such as the Space Shuttle Challenger disaster.

articles.title: The space of minds
articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy discusses the differences between animal and LLM intelligence, highlighting the distinct optimization pressures and objectives that shape their development.

articles.title: SEPs Are Moving to Pull Requests
articles.summary: SEPs (Model Context Protocol specifications) are now submitted as pull requests to the seps directory on GitHub, changing the contribution process for developers.

articles.title: Antigravity Grounded! Security Vulnerabilities in Google's Latest IDE
articles.summary: Google's Antigravity IDE contains security vulnerabilities, including some previously reported by Embrace The Red in May 2025. This matters because it highlights potential security risks in widely used AI development tools.

articles.title: One Year of MCP: November 2025 Spec Release
articles.summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has reached its one-year anniversary, and a new specification release is available for November 2025. This release matters as it updates the protocol for continued growth and adoption in the AI model ecosystem.

articles.title: MCP Apps: Extending servers with interactive user interfaces
articles.summary: The MCP Apps Extension proposal (SEP-1865) aims to standardize interactive user interfaces in MCP, developed with OpenAI and Anthropic. This matters because it could enable more user-friendly and interactive experiences with MCP servers.

articles.title: Adopting the MCP Bundle format (.mcpb) for portable local servers
articles.summary: The MCP Bundle format (.mcpb) is now part of the MCP project, allowing for one-click installation of local servers on compatible clients.

articles.title: Verifiability
articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy discusses the shift from Software 1.0 (hand-written programs) to Software 2.0 (AI-generated programs), highlighting verifiability as the key feature for tasks that can be optimized and automated.

articles.title: Server Instructions: Giving LLMs a user manual for your server
articles.summary: Server instructions provide context for LLMs to use MCP server tools effectively, giving them a user manual for the server.

articles.title: Claude Pirate: Abusing Anthropic's File API For Data Exfiltration
articles.summary: An attacker can use Anthropic's Claude model to exfiltrate user data via the File API, exploiting a new network request capability. This matters because it highlights a new vulnerability in a popular AI model, demonstrating the importance of secure design in AI systems.

articles.title: Animals vs Ghosts
articles.summary: Karpathy discusses the current state of LLM research, comparing it to building animals and summoning ghosts, and mentions Sutton's Dwarkesh pod. This matters because it provides insight into the current trends and directions in LLM research.

articles.title: Update on the Next MCP Protocol Release
articles.summary: The next MCP protocol release is delayed due to prioritization of new features and security improvements. This matters because it will impact the development and deployment of MCP-compliant models and applications.

articles.title: Cross-Agent Privilege Escalation: When Agents Free Each Other
articles.summary: Agents can be exploited to break out of their sandbox and execute arbitrary code by overwriting their configuration and security settings.

articles.title: Introducing the MCP Registry
articles.summary: The MCP Registry is a previewed open catalog and API for discovering publicly available MCP servers. This matters because it simplifies the process of finding and accessing MCP servers.

articles.title: Announcing the Official PHP SDK for MCP
articles.summary: The official PHP SDK for MCP is now generally available, built in collaboration with the PHP Foundation and Symfony.

articles.title: Wrap Up: The Month of AI Bugs
articles.summary: Multiple AI models, including ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, and GitHub Copilot, were found to be vulnerable to various attacks, including prompt injection, data exfiltration, and remote code execution. This matters because these vulnerabilities can compromise user data and allow attackers to execute arbitrary commands.

articles.title: AgentHopper: An AI Virus
articles.summary: AgentHopper is an AI virus concept that exploits vulnerabilities in popular agents, allowing remote code execution via indirect prompt injection. This matters because it highlights the potential for AI systems to be compromised and used for malicious purposes.

articles.title: Windsurf MCP Integration: Missing Security Controls Put Users at Risk
articles.summary: A security vulnerability was found in the Windsurf MCP integration, allowing users to be at risk due to missing security controls. This matters because it highlights the importance of empowering users to configure AI actions and review suggestions before execution.

articles.title: Cline: Vulnerable To Data Exfiltration And How To Protect Your Data
articles.summary: Cline AI coding agent is vulnerable to data exfiltration through markdown image rendering from untrusted domains, allowing prompt injection attacks. This matters because sensitive user information can be stolen.

articles.title: AWS Kiro: Arbitrary Code Execution via Indirect Prompt Injection
articles.summary: AWS Kiro, a coding agent, is vulnerable to arbitrary code execution via indirect prompt injection, allowing a remote attacker to hijack the agent and run custom code.

articles.title: How Prompt Injection Exposes Manus' VS Code Server to the Internet
articles.summary: A prompt injection attack exposed Manus' VS Code Server to the internet, allowing attackers to access it with a shared URL and password. This demonstrates a vulnerability in Manus' autonomous agent, highlighting potential security risks.

articles.title: How Deep Research Agents Can Leak Your Data
articles.summary: Deep Research agents can leak data between connected tools, such as web search and custom-built MCP servers, due to unmonitored access and interactions. This matters because it highlights a potential security risk in AI research agents.

articles.title: Sneaking Invisible Instructions by Developers in Windsurf
articles.summary: A vulnerability in Windsurf Cascade allows malicious instructions to be hidden in plain sight, invisible to developers but interpretable by LLMs, which can lead to prompt injection attacks. This matters because it highlights a new attack vector for malicious actors to manipulate AI systems.

articles.title: Windsurf: Memory-Persistent Data Exfiltration (SpAIware Exploit)
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a vulnerability in ChatGPT and OpenAI's models, allowing memory-persistent data exfiltration through the SpAIware attack. This matters because it highlights the potential for AI models to be exploited for malicious data extraction.

articles.title: Evolving OAuth Client Registration in the Model Context Protocol
articles.summary: MCP has adopted OAuth 2.1 as the foundation for its authorization framework, focusing on client registration for secure connections between clients and servers.

articles.title: MCP Prompts: Building Workflow Automation
articles.summary: The MCP Blog provides a practical guide to building workflow automation using MCP prompts and resource templates, demonstrated through a meal planning example.

articles.title: Building to Last: A New Governance Model for MCP
articles.summary: MCP introduces a formal governance model, including Specification Enhancement Proposals (SEPs), a maintainer structure, and a community-driven process for evolving the protocol.

articles.title: The Model Context Protocol Blog
articles.summary: The official Model Context Protocol blog is now live, featuring updates, tutorials, and insights from maintainers and contributors.

articles.title: Vibe coding MenuGen
articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy built MenuGen, a web app that generates images of menu items from a picture, using 100% code generated by Cursor+Claude. This is Karpathy's first end-to-end vibe coded app, demonstrating the feasibility of vibe coding for non-webdevs.

articles.title: Power to the people: How LLMs flip the script on technology diffusion
articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy notes that Large Language Models (LLMs) have flipped the script on technology diffusion, providing disproportionate benefits to individuals rather than corporations and governments, and attributes this to their ability to offer versatile but shallow expertise.

articles.title: Finding the Best Sleep Tracker
articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy compares the sleep tracking capabilities of four devices: Oura, Whoop, 8Sleep, and Apple Watch with AutoSleep. He finds Oura and Whoop to be the most accurate, with Oura offering a more dynamic range of scores.

articles.title: How I use LLMs
articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy shares how he uses Large Language Models in his daily life, covering various features and tools, from basic interactions to advanced data analysis and audio input/output.

articles.title: Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT
articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy provides a comprehensive deep dive into Large Language Models (LLMs), covering their development, 'psychology', and practical applications. This video aims to raise knowledge and understanding of the state-of-the-art in AI, empowering viewers to effectively use LLMs in their work.

articles.title: Let's reproduce GPT-2 (124M)
articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy reproduces GPT-2 (124M) from scratch in a YouTube video, covering network building, optimization, and training setup. This matters because it demonstrates the feasibility of replicating large language models with minimal external knowledge.

articles.title: Let's build the GPT Tokenizer
articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy builds the GPT Tokenizer from scratch, highlighting its importance and issues in Large Language Models. This matters because tokenization is a critical component of LLMs, and its problems can have significant impacts on model performance.

articles.title: [1hr Talk] Intro to Large Language Models
articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy gives a 1-hour introduction to Large Language Models, covering their basics, comparisons, and security challenges. This talk is a general-audience explanation of the technology behind systems like ChatGPT and Claude.

articles.summary: Karpathy builds a WaveNet architecture in his makemore series, exploring a tree-like structure and convolutional neural networks. This tutorial provides insight into the deep learning development process and PyTorch's torch.nn module.

articles.title: Building makemore Part 4: Becoming a Backprop Ninja
articles.summary: Karpathy manually backpropagates through a 2-layer MLP to understand how gradients flow through the compute graph, building intuition for neural net optimization.

articles.title: Building makemore Part 3: Activations & Gradients, BatchNorm
articles.summary: Karpathy explains the importance of activation and gradient statistics in deep neural networks, and introduces Batch Normalization as a key innovation that made training deep nets easier.

articles.title: Building makemore Part 2: MLP
articles.summary: Karpathy implements a multilayer perceptron (MLP) character-level language model and covers machine learning basics in a video. This matters because it provides a clear introduction to fundamental concepts in machine learning.

articles.summary: Karpathy introduces a bigram character-level language model, focusing on using torch.Tensor and the framework of language modeling, including training, sampling, and loss evaluation.

articles.title: Stable diffusion dreams of psychedelic faces
articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy created a video of psychedelic faces using Stable Diffusion, interpolating between randomly chosen noise vectors. This showcases the model's ability to generate diverse and creative images.

articles.title: Stable diffusion dreams of steampunk brains
articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy created a video using Stable Diffusion, interpolating between noise vectors to generate an image of a steampunk brain. This demonstrates the model's ability to produce high-quality images from a single prompt.

articles.title: Stable diffusion dreams of tattoos
articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy shares a video of Stable Diffusion generating images of tattoos, with some minor jumps due to NSFW content.

articles.title: The spelled-out intro to neural networks and backpropagation: building micrograd
articles.summary: Karpathy explains backpropagation and neural network training in a step-by-step, calculus-based tutorial, assuming basic Python knowledge.
